title: Deployment mode deliberation - Scallop Therapeutics POC kickoff
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC to validate hosting mode for a clinical-notes summarization feature. Main decision factors: latency (p99), throughput, data residency/compliance, cost per 1k tokens and operational ownership. Agreed benchmark plan: synthetic + shadow traffic runs week 2-3, security docs exchange, and an initial hosted pilot with a path to Dedicated or Private if needed.
topics: Workload sizing (qps, sequence lengths, KV cache expectations)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Samir to share hosted/dedicated pricing sheet and SSO/KMS checklist by 2026-11-13
Elena to propose benchmark harness and sample prompt set by 2026-11-15
Praiya Priya? (Priya) to share data residency constraints and SOC2 evidence link by 2026-11-14
Customer to provide representative traffic trace and sample docs for quality eval by 2026-11-18
Schedule benchmark kickoff (30-45m) for week of 2026-11-22
action_items: Samir Patel | Send hosted and dedicated pricing + terms | 2026-11-13
Elena Cho | Bench harness (stress + latency) plan + scripts | 2026-11-15
Priya Nair | Security requirements doc + SOC2 attestation link | 2026-11-14

transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): All right everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run 55, 60 minutes ish. Quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Maya Ross (Scallop): Hi, Maya here, head of ML, leading this effort. We're trying to ship a clinical summary feature for physicians, must keep PHI considerations in mind.
[00:24] Tom Fletcher (Scallop): Tom, infra lead. I'll scope network and on-prem pieces.
[00:28] Priya Nair (Scallop): Priya, security. I'll be focused on SOC2, KMS and audit logs.
[00:34] Luis Gomez (Scallop): Luis, product. I'm here for success criteria and timelines.
[00:38] Elena (Redwood SE): Elena from Redwood, I'll run through benchmarking and latency/cost tradeoffs.
[00:44] Samir: Cool. The goal today is: align on success criteria for the POC, size the workload, and pick initial hosting mode — hosted to move fast or Dedicated/Private if compliance or latency force it.
[00:59] Maya: High level: clinicians need sub-500ms median for short summaries, but more importantly p99 matters for UX. If p99 stretches beyond 1.5 seconds at peak it's problematic. Securitywise we need auditability and at-rest encryption.
[01:18] Elena: Helpful. For us, p99 under 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) is realistic on Dedicated, hosted can often hit ~400-600ms depending on model and concurrency. But depends on batching and KV caching.
[01:36] Tom: Important to surface what "short prompts" mean — our average input is about 600 tokens (full notes) but we expect to truncate / extract sections and run a summarization prompt that creates 80-150 token outputs. So sequence lengths variable.
[01:55] Elena: OK that's common — we'll want to benchmark with typical 600-token input and 120-token output. We'll also test a prefix-cached pattern: same patient header repeated across requests to measure KV reuse.
[02:12] Samir: Can I ask on throughput? what QPS are you sizing for initial pilot and long term?
[02:17] Luis: For pilot, peak 25 req/s, sustained around 8-10 req/s. Production target is 60 req/s peak, 20 sustained inside a containerized EHR traffic pattern.
[02:30] Elena: Noted — those numbers map to Dedicated pools or multi-tenant hosted burst capacity. Hosted could work for pilot but we'd want a Dedicated reservation for predictable p99 at scale.
[02:42] Priya: On data residency — all PHI must remain in our US-EAST region and logs must be retained for 12 months. We cannot have model weights or unencrypted data exit our VPC without an MOU.
[02:56] Samir: Understood. We support private deployments with a customer-controlled VPC and on-prem bundles; Dedicated can be placed in a single region with VPC peering and KMS integration. Hosted API supports regional tenancy but for strict VPC isolation we recommend Private.
[03:12] Maya: Timeline? we want to see a benchmark and quality results in 3 weeks, followed by a go/no-go for production in 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
[03:21] Elena: Yes — typical plan: week 1 onboarding and replay/traffic ingest, week 2 synthetic + shadow traffic benchmarking, week 3 quality evals and tuning. That lines up with a 6-week POC if both sides react quickly.
[03:36] Luis: Are there any automated fallbacks if the model goes slow? We can't have clinicians waiting.
[03:42] Elena: Canarying + fallback to a cheaper shorter-model or cached summary. Redwood supports routing policies: respond from a smaller model or cached summary when latency breaches SLO. We'll demo that in the benchmark.
[03:56] Tom: Cost targets — finance wants < $0.02 per 1k tokens for inference. Is that realistic?
[04:04] Samir: Depends on model/quantization and batching. Hosted with popular open models is often in $0.01-0.03 per 1k-token ballpark; Dedicated/Private can reduce unit cost but requires commitment. We'll send a cost comparison.
[04:16] Maya: Quality-wise we need ROUGE and clinician-graded scores. We'll provide 200 reference summaries. Can Redwood host the eval harness?
[04:25] Elena: Yes, we can run the evals on our infra or provide scripts for you to run locally. For the POC we'll run both to remove bias.
[04:33] Samir: Great. Let's talk hosting tradeoffs concretely. Elena, can you walk through the quick decision matrix?
[04:39] Elena: Sure. Hosted: fastest onboarding, no infra ops for you, good for pilot — tradeoffs are slightly higher and less isolation. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable p99 and lower unit cost at scale, sits in a cloud region with VPC peering and KMS — needs contract/commitment. Private: customer-managed VPC or on-prem — best for strict compliance/data residency, more setup time, higher TCO and ops responsibility.
[05:05] Luis: So if we value p99 and cost later, Dedicated makes sense. But for PHI, isn't Private required?
[05:12] Priya: Not necessarily. If Dedicated can provide VPC peering, customer-managed keys, and audit logs with SLAs, that may be acceptable. We need SOC2 evidence and a KMS integration that ensures Redwood never sees keys.
[05:25] Samir: We have a KMS integration pattern where customer keys are used to encrypt persistent storage; ephemeral caches use server-side keys. We'll include the design doc.
[05:33] Maya: We also need to understand failover across regions — if US-EAST has an outage, can we fail to another region without violating residency?
[05:41] Elena: Failover is policy-driven. For strict residency, we can prevent automatic failover across regions and instead have active-passive in the same region. If you want multi-region DR inside US zones, that's doable.
[05:53] Tom: Benchmark specifics — what metrics will you capture?
[05:57] Elena: We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, memory/KV hit rates, tokens/sec, cost per token, and a quality metric: ROUGE/clinician accuracy for summaries. We'll also capture tail latency under concurrency.
[06:12] Samir: For the benchmark harness, please include a shadow run with real traffic and a synthetic stress test. For KV caching, test with 20-40% repeat prefixes.
[06:23] Dr. Maya: On the model side, we are evaluating a Llama-variant at 13B quantized, and a smaller 7B distilled for fallback. Can Redwood serve both?
[06:33] Elena: Yes, Redwood can host multiple model variants and route between them. We'll recommend quantization profiles; 13B-8bit + optimized kernels often give the best latency/quality mix.
[06:43] Luis: Any concerns about tokenization or instruction-following differences in clinical text?
[06:47] Elena: We'll include tokenization checks. Clinical shorthand sometimes triggers tokenization bloat; we'll measure effective tokens and suggest prompt templates to reduce irrelevant context.
[06:55] Samir: Priya, anything blocking on legal/contract side for trying hosted for a pilot?
[07:00] Priya: If PHI is involved, we need a BAA. We can consider a limited dataset for hosted if de-identified; otherwise we need Dedicated with VPC peering or Private. So decision depends on how much PHI you want in the pilot.
[07:15] Samir: Understood. One option — run hosted initially using de-identified or synthetic data for the benchmark, then move to Dedicated or Private for any PHI runs. That keeps the timeline tight.
[07:26] Dr. Maya: That could work. We'll de-id a slice.
[07:30] Tom: On infra contacts — if we go Dedicated or Private, I need network diagrams and port lists. Samir, can you share that?
[07:36] Samir: Yes, we'll attach a VPC peering and firewall sheet.
[07:39] Elena: Regarding observability — Redwood Console exposes per-route latency and token cost, tracing hooks, and rollout controls. We'll show a demo during the benchmark kickoff.
[07:50] Luis: How do rollouts work if we switch model weights? We need canarying with percentage rollouts.
[07:55] Elena: We support percent rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions. Also A/B tests with traffic splitting.
[08:02] Priya: For audit logs and retention, can we get 12 months of request-level logs with redaction options?
[08:08] Samir: Yes — logs can be forwarded to your S3 endpoint with encryption and retention policies. We'll outline options.
[08:15] Dr. Maya: Let's define success criteria concretely so we can sign off. I propose: p99 < 800ms for the initial hosted benchmark with de-identified data; for production we need p99 < 350ms in Dedicated or equivalent SLA, quality > 0.75 clinician-accuracy on reference set, and cost under $0.02 per 1k tokens.
[08:39] Elena: Those are reasonable. We'll measure and report. If we can't hit p99 < 350ms on Dedicated, we'll explore caching, quantization, or Private options.
[08:49] Luis: If we agree to a Dedicated reservation, what's the lead time?
[08:52] Samir: Contractually around 2-3 weeks to provision a reserved pool, but we can use hosted capacity while setup is underway.
[08:59] Tom: For Private on-prem, what's typical setup time?
[09:02] Elena: On-prem takes longer — 4-8 weeks depending on access and approvals. That's a heavier lift.
[09:08] Priya: Any certifications for the on-prem package? We need an architecture review.
[09:12] Elena: We'll provide architecture docs and a security review checklist. Our private offering includes a hardened agent and audit hooks.
[09:20] Samir: Quick note — we sometimes see mismatch between synthetic benchmarks and real traffic due to session stickiness and KV cache; the shadow run is the best signal.
[09:30] Dr. Maya: We'll provide sampled live traffic for a shadow run with redaction.
[09:34] Elena: Great. For the bench harness we'll need: list of endpoints to target, sample prompts, concurrency patterns, and the token distribution. We'll draft that and send.
[09:45] Samir: OK wrapping toward next steps — we'll share: pricing, security checklist, VPC/firewall doc, and benchmark plan. You (customer) will share data samples and eval prompts. Then schedule benchmark kickoff week of 11/22.
[09:59] Luis: Sounds good. Any outstanding concerns?
[10:02] Priya: Just to reiterate — BAA and KMS control are must-haves before PHI hits hosted.
[10:08] Samir: Agreed. For the pilot we'll start with de-id hosted tests then move to Dedicated if PHI needed.
[10:14] Dr. Maya: OK. Thanks all.
[10:17] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with docs.
[10:22] Elena: I'll set up the benchmark repo and share access.
[10:26] Tom: I'll loop in network ops once we have the VPC diagram.
[10:30] Samir: Meeting notes will be shared. End.
[10:34] [end of recording - transcription may have small errors like speaker tags or punctuation]
